subject: Phased Capacity Commit + GPU Price Backstop — Luminary AI
messages:
From: Hannah Li <hannah.li@luminary.ai>
To: olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@luminary.ai
Date: Tue, 11 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial ask — phased reserved capacity + GPU price backstop

Olga,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Luminary's usage profile looks like: bursty inference for search rerank during business hours and steady background embedding loads overnight. We're interested in a reserved capacity contract but worried about 18–36 month GPU price volatility.

Quick ask: can Redwood propose a phased commit structure with an embedded price backstop (cap/floor or indexation) for committed SKUs? We'd prefer a 12-month ramp (60% year 1 / 30% year 2 / 10% optional year 3) and a mechanism to protect Luminary if GPU spot/market costs spike.

We're starting procurement review next week — curious what level of discount you'd need to offer that structure and what approval path looks like. Also attaching our projected monthly peak vCPU/GPU hours.

Attachments: peak_profile_jun28.csv

Best,
Hannah Li
Head of Platform — Luminary AI
H: +1 (415) 555-0182

From: olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Li <hannah.li@luminary.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 Jul 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask — phased reserved capacity + GPU price backstop

Hannah — thanks for the clear ask and the profile. I ran a quick look with Marcus on fleet implications. High-level thoughts:

- We can structure a phased commit (60/30/10) and price it as a blended reserved SKU rate with an explicit GPU-cost backstop tied to a published GPU index (quarterly).
- Tradeoff: deeper up-front discount requires a longer guaranteed commit or an escrow/contingency charge for downside protection.
- For Luminary's sizing the main lever is how much of the year-1 volume you commit upfront vs optional. That materially changes the unit price.

I'll attach a short proposal (RI_Phased_Commit_Proposal_v1.pdf) and a sensitivity model. High-level options we can offer:

1) Baseline: 12m firm (60% of projected peak) + 12m optional (30%) with 6m termination window. Discount: 20% off list reserved SKU; backstop: quarterly GPU index reconciliation, customer pays additional if index exceeds threshold.

2) Backstop-protected: 12m firm (60%) + 12m optional (30%) + 12m optional (10%) with 25% discount up-front, and a price protection cap — Redwood absorbs up to 8% GPU cost increase; beyond that, incremental pass-through with a shared split. Requires finance/exec ok.

3) Insurance-lite: smaller discount (15%) but escrow deposit equivalent to one month committed bill; refund if index stays within agreed band.

Next steps: I want to run the sensitivity model with Karthik and Marcus and come back with a recommended option and what approvals we need (finance + revenue ops + possibly Marcus for capacity). If that sounds good I'll get back by EOD Thursday with a recommended ask for discounts and approvals.

Olga Petrov
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
Direct: +1 (650) 555-0114
Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 12 Jul 2028 08:27:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Initial ask — phased reserved capacity + GPU price backstop

Team — quick internal notes after running the GPU sensitivity model attached by Olga. Summary:

- For Luminary's projected ramp, the baseline capacity (60% year 1) maps to ~28 A100-equivalent GPUs steady-state daytime with burst headroom. If they want the 30% year 2 optional to be effectively available, we should reserve an additional 12 GPUs in our pool or guarantee burst on pre-negotiated windows.
- Financial sensitivity: a 10% market GPU cost increase increases Redwood's marginal provisioning cost by ~13% once factoring in spot/maintenance overhead. That means our margin on a 20% discount baseline compresses by ~40% in that scenario.

Suggested internal approval path for option 2 (backstop-protected):
- Sales: Olga signs SOW with proposed pricing.
- Finance: Marcus to approve discount up to 25% and set escrow/buffer targets.
- Infra/Capacity: Grace to confirm the 12-GPU buffer and identify potential cross-customer pooling allowances.
- Execs: If GPU cost backstop liability > $250k over 12 months, bring to VP Sales for sign-off.

Attachments referenced: gpu_price_sensitivity_model.xlsx (scenario tabs: baseline / +10pc / +25pc)

I'll run the model for three price trajectories and return with recommended approved discount caps by Thursday COB.

— Karthik
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
From: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Hannah Li <hannah.li@luminary.ai>
Date: Thu, 14 Jul 2028 16:08:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Initial ask — phased reserved capacity + GPU price backstop

Hannah / team — looping in finance and capacity confirmation. Short answer: we can offer Option 2 (Backstop-protected) with the following guardrails:

- Agreed committed ramp: 60% (12m firm) / 30% (12m option) / 10% (12m optional) as term milestones in SOW.
- Price: 24% discount vs list for the committed baseline, subject to GPU index reconciliation quarterly. Redwood will absorb up to an 8% increase in the GPU index for the committed portion; above that, pass-through split 60% customer / 40% Redwood on incremental GPU cost.
- Capacity: Redwood to reserve an explicit buffer of 12 GPUs in the same region (us-west) and offer scheduled burst windows. We will retain the right to shift burst outside Luminary's peak windows with 72h notice.
- Financial safeguards: 2-month escrow deposit equal to expected committed baseline bill for 3 months; refundable per contract milestones.

I will prepare a short amendment and SOW language and send to Procurement (copied) for redlines. This offer requires VP Sales notification if Luminary asks to increase the discount beyond 26% or change the pass-through split materially.

Marcus Lin
Director, Revenue Finance — Redwood Inference
Attachments: RI_Phased_Commit_Proposal_v1.pdf, gpu_price_sensitivity_model.xlsx

On procurement next steps: Hannah, if you can share a preferred SOW template and key legal points, Procurement can accept our amendment language and we can move to signatures mid-next-week.
